# OpenCode2API-Proxy [![License: GPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPLv3-blue.svg)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/opencode2api-proxy.svg?logo=npm&logoColor=white)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode2api-proxy) [![CI](https://github.com/IMROVOID/OpenCode2API/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/IMROVOID/OpenCode2API/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![Node.js Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-%3E%3D26.0.0-339933?logo=node.js&logoColor=white)](https://nodejs.org/) [![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-7.0.2-3178C6?logo=typescript&logoColor=white)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) [![Cloudflare Workers](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cloudflare-Workers-F38020?logo=cloudflare&logoColor=white)](https://workers.cloudflare.com/) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCode-FF6900?logo=opencode&logoColor=white)](https://opencode.ai/) [![OpenAI Compatible](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAI-Compatible-412991?logo=openai&logoColor=white)](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference)

OpenCode Zen and Go to a universal OpenAI, Responses and Anthropic compatible API router. Serve Zen and Go models from one endpoint with protocol conversion, streaming, key rotation, rich model attributes, and a built-in control WebUI with AI Chat and one-click self-updating.

## Table of Contents - [What is OpenCode2API-Proxy?](#what-is-opencode2api-proxy) - [Why OpenCode2API?](#why-opencode2api) - [Key Features](#key-features) - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Method 1: Local Daemon & npm](#method-1-local-daemon--npm) - [Method 2: Built Release](#method-2-built-release) - [Method 3: Cloudflare Workers (Serverless)](#method-3-cloudflare-workers-serverless) - [Method 4: Docker & Self-Hosted (Coolify / Dokploy / Zeabur)](#method-4-docker--self-hosted-coolify--dokploy--zeabur) - [Model Catalog & Aliases](#model-catalog--aliases) - [Client Integration](#client-integration) - [Architecture & Structure](#architecture--structure) - [Advanced Guides](#advanced-guides) - [WebUI Control Panel & AI Chat Suite](#webui-control-panel--ai-chat-suite) - [Automatic Update System](#automatic-update-system) - [Protocol Conversion](#protocol-conversion) - [Key Rotation & Failure Handling](#key-rotation--failure-handling) - [Unlimited Lane & Dual-Lane Architecture](#unlimited-lane--dual-lane-architecture) - [Environment Variables](#environment-variables) - [Development & Testing](#development--testing) - [Continuous Integration (CI)](#continuous-integration-ci) - [Building & Publishing Releases](#building--publishing-releases) - [Disclaimer & Legal Notice](#disclaimer--legal-notice) - [References & Acknowledgements](#references--acknowledgements) - [License](#license) ## What is OpenCode2API-Proxy? [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/) serves its **Zen** and **Go** model families behind two different wire shapes. The Zen lane expects the OpenCode 1.x request format, the Go lane the OpenCode 2.x CLI format, and neither is directly consumable by the OpenAI-compatible clients developers actually use. **OpenCode2API-Proxy** bridges that gap: 1. It discovers the models OpenCode publishes, per tier, and learns each model's **native protocol** and **rich attributes** (context windows, limits, modalities, capabilities) from OpenCode's own capability catalog. 2. It serves a single endpoint that speaks **OpenAI Chat Completions**, **OpenAI Responses** and **Anthropic Messages** at the same time, converting a request from the client's protocol to the upstream's and converting the answer back. 3. It rotates across several upstream keys, cools down the ones that fail, and falls back from the anonymous lane to the authenticated tiers. 4. It ships an advanced **control WebUI & AI Chat Suite** with System, Dark, and Light themes on every deployment method, featuring streaming chat inference, IDE-style document previews, 30-day stateless sessions, and a one-click Cloudflare Worker self-updater. > **Note**: The Go lane requires an active OpenCode Go subscription and a workspace in the Global region. The free tier is served from the official OpenCode client only, so it needs that client's TLS fingerprint. See [Disclaimer & Legal Notice](#disclaimer--legal-notice). > **Reference**: Inspired by and referencing the original [jasonxu114514/opencode2api](https://github.com/jasonxu114514/opencode2api) repository. ## Why OpenCode2API? If you are looking to plug OpenCode Zen and Go models into **Cursor, Claude Code, Cline, Roo Code, or OpenWebUI**, here is how `IMROVOID/OpenCode2API` compares to standard wrappers and forks: | Feature / Pain Point | Basic CLI Wrappers & Competing Repos | `IMROVOID/OpenCode2API` | | --- | --- | --- | | **Protocol Coverage** | OpenAI `/v1/chat/completions` only | **Triple Protocol:** Native OpenAI Chat, `/v1/responses` (reasoning/streams), and native **Anthropic `/v1/messages`** | | **Runtime Footprint** | Requires global Node.js + OpenCode CLI subprocess | Single self-contained binary, 1-command Docker / npm, or zero-local-dependency Cloudflare Worker bundle | | **Rate Limits & 429s** | Dies when anonymous IP quota hits | Automatic proxy/key pooling, exponential cooldown circuit breakers, DoH IPv6 edge pool rotation, and Kilo tier failover | | **Tool Calling & Streaming** | Often breaks on SSE or tool schemas | Full native tool-call translation, structured reasoning tokens, and first-event SSE timeout protection | | **Context Window Preservation** | Truncates to 200k/256k | Auto-detects and preserves full **1,000,000 token context windows** without down-tiering | | **Control Plane** | None (headless terminal logs) | Full-featured Control WebUI & AI Chat Suite with Light/Dark themes, file preview, metrics, and one-click self-updating | ## Key Features - **Three Protocols, One Endpoint**: `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses` and `/v1/messages` all accept the same request body and answer in the protocol the client asked for. - **Three Deployment Methods**: - **Local Daemon & npm**: Run globally via npm (`npm install -g opencode2api-proxy`), run directly with `npx`, or run from a cloned repository with a local API endpoint on `127.0.0.1:8080` and control WebUI on `127.0.0.1:8081`. - **Built Release**: Cross-platform ZIP archives for Linux, Windows and macOS on x64 and arm64, each with an example configuration. - **Cloudflare Worker**: A standalone bundle with no Node built-ins, full control WebUI, and self-healing rotation. - **Advanced WebUI & AI Chat Suite**: - **Interactive AI Chat Panel**: Real-time SSE streaming inference, tool call execution visualization, live process indicator, message jump navigation, timeline groups, and search highlighting. - **In-Place Markdown Composer**: Rich-text composer with custom formatting context menu and custom modal hyperlink overlay (zero browser alert popups). - **File Preview Panel**: Responsive split-pane and mobile overlay preview panel for text, Markdown, HTML, CSV, and PDF documents with segmented Preview / IDE raw mode, line numbers gutter, and download menu. - **Draft & Staging Persistence**: Unsent messages, conversation preview panel states, and media staging persist in `localStorage` across reloads with edge gradient fades. - **Theme Switcher**: System (default), Dark, and Light mode switcher with upward combobox menu, SVG icons, greyscale OKLCH tokens, and `localStorage` persistence. - **Instant Skeleton Loading**: Instant route skeleton states and smooth horizontal sliding sidebar collapse animation. - **Interactive Monitor & Charts**: Real-time request counters, latency tracking, uptime scales (days/weeks/months/years), and SVG charts. - **Automatic Update Checker & One-Click Cloudflare Worker Updater**: - Checks GitHub Releases and npm registry on a 15-minute cache with in-panel release notes preview. - One-click remote update for Cloudflare Workers using a scoped Cloudflare API token (`workers:write`). - Automatic update commands for Node.js git repos (`git pull --ff-only && npm run build`) and npm global installs. - **Robust 30-Day Stateless Sessions & Persistence**: - HMAC-SHA256 signed stateless session tokens in HTTP-only cookies (`opencode2api_session`) surviving Worker cold-starts. - Server state sidecar persistence (`.opencode2api-state.json`) for local daemon sessions, metrics, and logs. - SPA routing with history navigation, preserving custom paths (`WEBUI_PATH` / `ADMIN_PATH`) without reload logout. - **Model Catalog Discovery & Rich Attributes**: - Discovers models on Zen and Go tiers and learns native protocols, context window lengths, token limits, and input/output modalities. - Exposes detailed descriptors on both daemon and Worker `/v1/models` endpoints. - Preserves 1M context windows without down-tiering in free equivalents. - **Protocol-Native Routing**: A request is sent in the upstream's own protocol, so no conversion happens on the hot path unless the client asked for a different one. - **Key Rotation & Cooldown**: A 401, 403 or 429 rotates to the next key of the tier; the failing key is cooled down with an exponential backoff, and a non-retryable 4xx leaves the tier immediately. - **Dual-Lane Self-Healing & Quota Bypass**: - **OpenCode Unlimited Lane**: Discovers live Cloudflare `AAAA` edge pools via DoH (`1.1.1.1/dns-query`), steers Worker subrequests with `cf.resolveOverride`, rotates device/session/project identities on `QuotaExceeded` / `429` walls (up to 8 hops), and blacklists burned `/64` prefixes. - **Kilo Free Gateway Failover**: Seamless secondary fallback to high-throughput free models without quotas, automatically rotating past 400 `context_length_exceeded`, 401, 403, and 404 errors while prioritizing 1M models. - **Full SSE Streaming**: Reasoning deltas, tool call arguments and the usage report survive the trip, and a non-streaming client gets the same answer collapsed back into one document. - **Complete Vector Branding Suite**: Parametric SVG logo marks, favicons, Apple touch icons, PWA icons, 1200x630 banner, and full OpenGraph/Twitter SEO metadata. - **Modern Toolchains & Quality**: - Built with **TypeScript 7.0.2** and **Node.js 26 LTS**. - **277 automated unit & integration tests** across 85 test suites. - **Standalone Public Website & Documentation Portal**: - Accessible at [opencode2api.rovoid.tech](https://opencode2api.rovoid.tech). - Visible Grid aesthetic with responsive interactive dot grid, fluid cursor, and full dark/light theme toggle. - Interactive Cloudflare Worker automated deployer with live subdomain and URL reporting. - Comprehensive documentation portal with instant search, keyboard shortcuts (`Ctrl+K`), and live code snippets. - **Safe & Resource-Bounded**: - 32 MB request body limit and 64 MB response body limit. - Client disconnect cancellation through `AbortSignal`. - An upstream timeout that ends a stalled request instead of hanging it. - Secrets masked out of every log line and every WebUI view. ## Quick Start ### Method 1: Local Daemon & npm #### Step 1: Get an API Key Create a key in the [OpenCode Console](https://opencode.ai/) and copy it. You need a key for the **Zen** tier, the **Go** tier, or both. #### Step 2: Install or Run Choose one of three ways to run: **Option A: Global npm Installation** ```bash npm install -g opencode2api-proxy ``` The package ships the CLI bundle, the standalone Cloudflare Worker bundle (`worker/worker.js`), and the example configuration. **Option B: Direct execution via npx (no install)** ```bash npx opencode2api-proxy start ``` **Option C: Clone from GitHub & build from source** ```bash git clone https://github.com/IMROVOID/OpenCode2API.git cd OpenCode2API npm install npm run build node dist/cli.js start ``` #### Step 3: Configure Copy the example configuration and edit it: ```bash cp config.example.json config.json ``` ```json { "listen": "127.0.0.1:8080", "server_keys": ["sk-your-local-key"], "zen_keys": ["sk-your-zen-key"], "go_keys": ["sk-your-go-key"], "webui": { "enabled": true, "listen": "127.0.0.1:8081", "username": "admin", "password": "change-this-admin-password" } } ``` `server_keys` are the keys your clients authenticate with. `zen_keys` and `go_keys` are the keys OpenCode issued you. Alternatively, provide keys directly via a `.env` file in your working directory without editing JSON: ```env API_KEY=sk-your-local-key OPENCODE_ZEN_KEYS=sk-your-zen-key OPENCODE_GO_KEYS=sk-your-go-key ``` #### Step 4: Start the Router ```bash opencode2api-proxy start ``` Or specify a custom port and key: ```bash opencode2api-proxy start --port 8080 --key sk-my-secret-key ``` Your local endpoint is available at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1`, and the control WebUI at `http://127.0.0.1:8081`. ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-your-local-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"deepseek-v4.1-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}' ``` ### Method 2: Built Release Prebuilt archives for every supported platform are attached to each release. #### Step 1: Download Grab the archive that matches your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/IMROVOID/OpenCode2API/releases): | Target | File | |---|---| | Linux x64 | `opencode2api-proxy-v1.2.0-linux-x64.zip` | | Linux arm64 | `opencode2api-proxy-v1.2.0-linux-arm64.zip` | | Windows x64 | `opencode2api-proxy-v1.2.0-win-x64.zip` | | Windows arm64 | `opencode2api-proxy-v1.2.0-win-arm64.zip` | | macOS (Intel) | `opencode2api-proxy-v1.2.0-macos-x64.zip` | | macOS (Apple Silicon) | `opencode2api-proxy-v1.2.0-macos-arm64.zip` | #### Step 2: Extract and configure ```bash unzip opencode2api-proxy-v1.2.0-linux-x64.zip -d opencode2api-proxy cd opencode2api-proxy mv config.example.json config.json ``` Each archive ships a **separate example configuration** named `config.example.json`, so the proxy never overwrites a configuration you already wrote. Rename it to `config.json` and fill in your keys. #### Step 3: Run ```bash node opencode2api-proxy.js ``` On Windows: ```powershell node opencode2api-proxy.js ``` The archive runs on any system with **Node.js 26 or newer**. Install it from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/) if you do not have it. ### Method 3: Cloudflare Workers (Serverless) Deploy a 24/7 serverless gateway without keeping your computer running. #### Step 1: Copy the Code Open [`worker/worker.js`](./worker/worker.js) and copy the entire file contents. #### Step 2: Create Worker in Cloudflare Dashboard 1. Log into the [Cloudflare Dashboard](https://dash.cloudflare.com). 2. Go to **Workers & Pages** -> **Create application** -> **Create Worker**. 3. Set name to `opencode2api-proxy` and click **Deploy**. 4. Click **Edit code**, select all existing code, delete it, and paste the copied contents of `worker/worker.js`. 5. Click **Deploy** in the top right. #### Step 3: Add Variables & Secrets In your Worker, go to **Settings** -> **Variables and Secrets** and configure as needed: | Variable | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `ADMIN_USERNAME` | Text / Secret | `admin` | Username for the control WebUI | | `ADMIN_PASSWORD` / `WEBUI_PASSWORD` | Secret | `admin` | Password for the control WebUI (change from default in production!) | | `WEBUI_PAT …[文件过长——中段 8KB 抽样]… , and auto-detects **rich attributes** (context window lengths, token limits, input/output modalities, and capabilities). Full **1M context windows** are preserved without down-tiering in free equivalents. You always request a **model id**, and the router picks the lane and the protocol. | Requested model | Lane | Notes | |---|---|---| | `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | Zen or Go | Served by the tier that advertises it. | | `glm-5.3` | Zen or Go | Served by the tier that advertises it. | | `grok-4.6` | Zen or Go | Served by the tier that advertises it. | | `kimi-k3` | Zen or Go | Served by the tier that advertises it. | | `qwen3.8-max` | Zen or Go | Served by the tier that advertises it. | | `claude-haiku-5-5` | Zen or Go | Native protocol is Anthropic Messages. | | `*free` | Anonymous | Served on the anonymous lane when it is enabled. | `GET /v1/models` lists everything the router can serve on both local daemon and Cloudflare Worker, including native protocols, context window limits, input/output modalities, and capabilities: ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-your-local-key" ``` ## Client Integration
Cursor & Windsurf IDE Use OpenCode Zen & Go models inside Cursor as your primary coding and agent model: 1. Open **Cursor Settings** (`Ctrl+,` or `Cmd+,`) -> **Models**. 2. Under **OpenAI API Key**, toggle custom API key and click **Override OpenAI Base URL**. 3. Set URL and Key: - **Base URL**: `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` (or your Cloudflare Worker URL `https://your-worker.workers.dev/v1`) - **API Key**: `sk-your-local-key` (or dummy string if `API_KEY` is not set) 4. Add model IDs: `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `glm-5.3`, `kimi-k3`, `qwen3.8-max`, `claude-haiku-5-5`. 5. Enable them in the model dropdown to code with full tool calling and streaming.
Claude Code CLI Point Anthropic's official terminal coding agent (`claude`) at your OpenCode router via native `/v1/messages`: ```bash export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:8080" export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="sk-your-local-key" export ANTHROPIC_MODEL="claude-haiku-5-5" # or deepseek-v4.1-flash / glm-5.3 claude ```
Cline, Roo Code & Continue.dev In VS Code extension settings, select **OpenAI Compatible** or **Anthropic Compatible**: ```json { "apiProvider": "openai", "openaiApiBase": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1", "openaiApiKey": "sk-your-local-key", "openaiModelId": "deepseek-v4.1-flash", "contextWindow": 1000000 } ``` *Note: OpenCode2API preserves full 1M context windows without truncation or forced down-tiering.*
OpenWebUI, LibreChat & SillyTavern Configure as a custom OpenAI-compatible provider. The gateway serves dynamic model listings with rich attributes via `/v1/models`: ```bash OPENAI_API_BASE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1" OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-your-local-key" ```
Python SDKs (OpenAI & Anthropic) **OpenAI Python SDK:** ```python from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI( base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1", api_key="sk-your-local-key", ) response = client.chat.completions.create( model="deepseek-v4.1-flash", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a binary search in Python."}], stream=True, ) for chunk in response: print(chunk.choices[0].delta.content or "", end="") ``` **Anthropic Python SDK:** ```python from anthropic import Anthropic client = Anthropic( base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8080", api_key="sk-your-local-key", ) message = client.messages.create( model="claude-haiku-5-5", max_tokens=1024, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain SSE streaming."}], ) print(message.content[0].text) ```
Codex CLI ```toml # ~/.codex/config.toml model = "deepseek-v4.1-flash" model_provider = "opencode2api" [model_providers.opencode2api] name = "OpenCode2API" base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1" env_key = "OPENCODE2API_KEY" wire_api = "responses" ```
OpenCode CLI ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "provider": { "opencode2api": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "options": { "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1", "apiKey": "sk-your-local-key" }, "models": { "deepseek-v4.1-flash": { "name": "DeepSeek v4.1 Flash" } } } }, "model": "opencode2api/deepseek-v4.1-flash" } ```
Cherry Studio / LobeChat / NextChat Add a custom OpenAI provider: | Field | Value | |---|---| | API address | `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` | | API key | `sk-your-local-key` | | Model | `deepseek-v4.1-flash` |
Any OpenAI-compatible client Point the client at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` and use `sk-your-local-key` as the API key. Every OpenAI-compatible client works, because the router speaks the client's protocol.

Check unlimited lane & guard health curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/unlimited/doctor \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-your-local-key" # Manually hop to a fresh edge and device/session identity curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/unlimited/hop \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-your-local-key" ``` ### Environment Variables Both the local daemon and Cloudflare Worker support environment variables. The local daemon automatically loads `.env` from the current working directory: | Variable | Target | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `OPENCODE2API_CONFIG` | Local | `./config.json` | Path to local JSON configuration file | | `API_KEY` / `API_KEYS` | Both | *(None)* | Client authorization bearer token(s), comma-separated. Also accepts `OPENCODE2API_SERVER_KEY` or `SERVER_KEYS`. | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_KEYS` | Both | *(None)* | Upstream OpenCode Zen keys, comma-separated. Also accepts `ZEN_KEYS` or `ZEN_KEY`. | | `OPENCODE_GO_KEYS` | Both | *(None)* | Upstream OpenCode Go keys, comma-separated. Also accepts `GO_KEYS` or `GO_KEY`. | | `OPENCODE_KEYS` | Both | *(None)* | Generic OpenCode keys, automatically classified into Zen or Go based on key prefix/content. | | `ADMIN_USERNAME` | Both | `admin` | Username for the control WebUI | | `ADMIN_PASSWORD` / `WEBUI_PASSWORD` | Both | `admin` | Password for the control WebUI (change from default in production!) | | `WEBUI_PATH` / `ADMIN_PATH` | Both | `/` | Web path where the control panel is served (e.g. `/admin`). ### Continuous Integration (CI) Every commit and pull request runs automated verification through the [Test & Verify](.github/workflows/test.yml) GitHub Actions workflow (Node.js 26 LTS and TypeScript 7): - **Typecheck**: `npm run typecheck` - **Unit & Integration Tests**: `npm test` (266 automated tests across 78 suites) - **Bundle Verification**: `npm run build`, plus a check that the Worker bundle carries no Node built-in. #### Skipping Automated Tests To skip the test suite on specific commits (e.g. for docs updates, asset additions, or fast iterations while still verifying types and builds), include any of the following tags in the commit message: - `[skip test]` or `[skip tests]` - `[skip-test]` or `[skip-tests]` When triggered manually via **Actions** -> **Run workflow**, check the **Skip running automated tests** input option. ### Building & Publishing Releases The [Release workflow](.github/workflows/release.yml) builds multi-arch platform binaries and the standalone Cloudflare Worker bundle, publishing them as a **Draft Release** on GitHub. #### Trigger Options 1. **Manual Trigger (`workflow_dispatch`)**: - Go to **Actions** -> **Release** -> **Run workflow**. - **Tag**: Release tag (defaults to `v` + `version` from `package.json`, e.g. `v1.2.0`). - **Draft**: Create as Draft release (defaults to `true`). Uncheck when ready to publish publicly. - **Overwrite**: If a release or tag with this name already exists, delete and recreate it (defaults to `true`). - **Custom Release Notes**: Optional markdown text to use as release notes. Leave empty to use GitHub's auto-generated release notes. - **Skip tests**: Check to bypass test execution during release packaging. 2. **Automatic Trigger via Commit Flag**: - Push a commit to `master` containing `[release]`, `[draft-release]`, or `[release-draft]` in the commit message. - Automatically builds and publishes a Draft release for the current `package.json` version. #### Release Assets Each release attaches: - 6 platform ZIP archives: `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `win-x64`, `win-arm64`, `macos-x64`, `macos-arm64`. - Standalone Cloudflare Worker script: `worker.js` (evaluated and pre-tested).
